sentences.text: Bow and beam is one case of a general rule called doubling the angle on the bow.
Whenever an object’s angle on the bow doubles, the distance run between the two bearings equals your distance from the object at the second bearing.
With thirty and sixty degrees, the distance run equals your distance off at the sixty degree bearing.

A useful extra: with twenty-two and a half and forty-five degrees, your distance off when you pass abeam will be about seven tenths of the distance run, which warns you early if you’ll pass too close.
